note: Round-69 GitHub global security advisories REST reference. S103 is GitHub Docs' own REST reference page for the two global-advisory endpoints (GET /advisories list with its query filters, GET /advisories/{ghsa_id}) at REST API version 2026-03-10: the read interface over the GitHub Advisory Database's reviewed, unreviewed and malware advisories. It is NOT the repository security advisories REST API the lane already holds (F36/S087; that capture's own page names global advisories as a separate reference) and not any advisory instance (S068). A second candidate, ENISA's EUVD API documentation at https://euvd.enisa.europa.eu/apidoc, was opened the same round and refused as an entry source for now: the served HTML is a 3062-byte single-page-application shell whose documentation text exists only after JavaScript rendering (bundle /static/js/main.61fcf30f.js, 544337 bytes in 2 lines, minified; receipt .ufo/waves/round-69/controls/euvd-refusal-r69.txt), so capture-source.py cannot produce a line-anchored snapshot; flip condition: a statically served or line-anchorable rendering of the same documentation.

sources.fetch_method: capture-source.py --kind html, default instrument UA (tags stripped, entities decoded, whitespace collapsed per line)

quotes.quote: Use the REST API to view global security advisories.
If no other parameters are defined, the request will return only GitHub-reviewed advisories that are not malware.
By default, all responses will exclude advisories for malware, because malware are not standard vulnerabilities.
Can be one of: reviewed, malware, unreviewed
Can be one of: rubygems, npm, pip, maven, nuget, composer, go, rust, erlang, actions, pub, other, swift
Can be one of: unknown, low, medium, high, critical
A maximum of 1000 packages can be specified.
The EPSS percentage represents the likelihood of a CVE being exploited.
The number of results per page (max 100).
Can be one of: updated, published, epss_percentage, epss_percentile
This endpoint can be used without authentication if only public resources are requested.
Gets a global security advisory using its GitHub Security Advisory (GHSA) identifier.
